title: DWTS Star’s Disney Night Wardrobe Malfunction Sparks Viral Buzz on Entertainment Weekly
body:
Amber Glenn’s glittering “Hercules” quickstep on *Dancing with the Stars* took an unexpected turn on Monday’s Disney Night when a strap on her costume gave way, briefly exposing the Olympian‑turned‑skater. The mishap unfolded mid‑performance, prompting a swift adjustment by Glenn and partner Pasha Pashkov and a flurry of reactions from the studio audience and viewers at home.

The 27‑year‑old former figure skater, who has been praised for her athleticism and poise since joining the competition, was dressed in a flowing, gold‑laminated gown designed to evoke the mythic heroine of the Disney classic. As the pair executed a rapid series of turns and lifts to a remix of “A Star Is Born” from *Hercules*, the dress’s side strap slipped, momentarily revealing a flash of skin before Glenn deftly pulled the fabric back into place. The incident lasted only a second, but the camera caught the slip, and social media lit up with memes, GIFs and supportive comments from fans and fellow contestants alike.

Costume malfunctions are not unheard of on live dance shows, yet they are relatively rare on *DWTS*, which typically employs a team of designers, stylists and riggers to ensure every garment can withstand the rigorous choreography. The show’s production team released a brief statement after the episode, acknowledging the glitch and confirming that the outfit will be reinforced for future performances. “We are proud of Amber’s professionalism and quick thinking in handling the situation,” the note read, adding that safety and comfort remain top priorities for all participants.

Glenn’s handling of the incident has drawn commendation from both the dance community and the broader public. Former *DWTS* champion Jordan Fisher tweeted, “Amber just turned a wardrobe slip into a power move—still flawless!” Meanwhile, veteran choreographer Derek Hough praised the duo’s resilience, noting that live television demands the ability to adapt on the fly. “In a perfect world, nothing ever goes wrong,” he said in a post‑show interview, “but the true test is how you recover, and Amber and Pasha showed exactly that.”

The episode’s ratings reflected the audience’s continued appetite for the show’s blend of nostalgia and competition. Disney Night, a themed segment that pairs iconic songs and costumes with elaborate storytelling, has become a staple of the season, drawing higher viewership numbers than the average episode. Analysts suggest that the added drama of a live mishap may have contributed to a modest spike in streaming and social engagement, underscoring how unscripted moments can amplify a program’s cultural footprint.

Looking ahead, Glenn and Pasha are slated to perform a Latin routine inspired by *Moana* in the next week, and producers have confirmed that the new costume will undergo additional testing to prevent a repeat. As the competition narrows and the stakes rise, the pair’s ability to maintain composure under pressure could prove decisive. Whether the brief wardrobe slip will linger in the public memory or simply become a footnote in the season’s narrative remains to be seen, but one thing is clear: Amber Glenn’s poise under the spotlight has only reinforced her reputation as a formidable contender on the dance floor.
